chapter.title: Estimation, Hypothesis Tests and Confidence Procedures

sections.title: Sampling models, estimands, statistics and identifiability

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C008 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful is not supplied. The argument that no level-1/2 test is most powerful against both p=1/4 and p=3/4 writes out only the p=3/4 maximization (annex 264-269). The p=1/4 half is waved through as 'the reversed calculation' (annex 270-272), a similarly-type appeal in place of the owed step. That half is: power (3/4)a+(1/4)b=(1/4)(a+b)+(1/2)a <= 3/4 under a+b <= 1, with equality only at a=1, b=0.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C013 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.neyman.interval.construction is not supplied. The proof needs a finite upper endpoint u(x) to belong to S(x), both for S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] intersected with R and for the upper-endpoint case of the source's Proposition VII (Neyman 1937 p. 355). That step is waved through with 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)' (annex 445-446). Only the lower-endpoint argument is written (annex 439-444).

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C016 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.confidence.coverage is not supplied. The upper-endpoint half of the exact inversion is waved through with 'Similarly ... for k=n, both are false' (annex 593-600). That half is p > u_n(k) iff F_{n,p}(k) < d for k<n, from F decreasing strictly with F_{n,u_n(k)}(k)=d, plus both conditions failing at k=n because u_n(n)=1 and F_{n,p}(n)=1>d. Both the inversion claim and the coverage bound of at least 1-alpha (annex 609-621) depend on this unwritten half.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C017 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.beta.quantiles is not supplied. The upper-limit formula u_n(k)=Q_{k+1,n-k}(1-d) depends on the lower-tail identity F_{n,p}(k)=1-I_p(k+1,n-k) for k<n. That identity is only asserted with 'Likewise' (annex 690-694). Neither route to it is written: F_{n,p}(k)=1-T_{n,p}(k+1) combined with the upper-tail identity at k+1, or derivative matching with value 1 at p=0. Only the upper-tail identity behind the lower-limit formula is derived (annex 677-689).
